title: Maximum Even Subsequence Sum
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers. Choose a subsequence of the array (any subset of its elements) so that the **sum of the chosen elements is even**, and make that sum as large as possible.

Values may be negative or zero. Choosing no elements at all is allowed and gives sum `0`, which is even, so an answer always exists.

Print the maximum possible even sum.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0..n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum even sum of a subsequence.

examples.explanation: Taking everything gives 19, which is odd. Dropping the smallest odd element (1) gives 18, and no even sum above 18 is reachable.
The positive elements sum to 11 (odd). Dropping 9 leaves only 2, but adding the negative odd element -1 instead gives 11 - 1 = 10, which is better.
Taking 7 alone is odd. Dropping it gives 0, but adding the larger of the negative odd elements, -3, gives 7 - 3 = 4, which is even and better. Adding -9 as well would only lower the sum.

hints: Ignoring parity, the best subsequence takes every positive element. When is that sum already even?
If the sum of the positives is odd, the parity must be flipped by changing exactly one odd element: either remove the smallest odd positive or add the largest odd non-positive element.
Alternatively run a DP over the array that keeps the best subsequence sum for each parity (even and odd) of the elements seen so far.
